_instructions: Copy this file to ~/.claude/settings.json (or merge it into your existing one).
Replace every <ROOT> placeholder with the absolute path to your workspace root.
Replace <YOUR-TRACKER-HUB-PATH> with the absolute path to your tracker hub (on a single-repo start this is simply <ROOT>/Claude).

Replace <YOUR-USER> in the deny rules with your OS user name. The deny examples are Windows-shaped (credential stores, DPAPI keys, browser profile data); on macOS or Linux, swap in your platform's equivalents (for example //Users/<YOUR-USER>/Library/Keychains/**). Deny rules use gitignore-style patterns; a leading // anchors at the filesystem root.
The Stop hook passes the write-back gate its two paths via env vars on the command line - filling THIS file configures that gate completely; the script-level placeholders are a backstop only.
The git gate lives at hooks/git-gate.mjs and fails closed; open it and replace <YOUR-HARD-LINES> with the push and commit constraints that apply in your workspace.

The env block caps runaway loops. The harness defaults are 200 subagent spawns and 200 web searches per session; the template ships 25 and 50. Raise them per-session for a sanctioned big run ($env:CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_SUBAGENTS_PER_SESSION = '100' before launching) instead of raising the standing cap.
The ask rule on Agent(model:opus) surfaces premium-tier subagent spawns for approval instead of letting them run silently; add one rule per premium tier you pay for.
The hooks block is the governance wiring; preference settings regenerate from use.
The git gate's command detection is regex-based and best-effort - a speed bump, not a security boundary; pair it with permission rules for anything that must be impossible.
